title: NGC 6302
caption: The Butterfly Nebula (NGC 6302), imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This Hubble image shows NGC 6302, better known as the Butterfly Nebula, a glowing cloud of gas within our Milky Way in the constellation of Scorpius.

The glowing gas once formed the outer layers of a star. Over about 2,200 years it has been cast off into space, building the butterfly shape. The nebula is a planetary nebula, the name astronomers give to gas thrown off by a Sun-like star near the end of its life. Despite the name, planetary nebulae have nothing to do with planets.

New observations have revealed unprecedented complexity in the nebula, and the jets and gas bubbles streaming from the star at its centre are changing quickly. The image uses several filters, including ones in near-infrared light and others tuned to the glow of particular gases.
scale: The nebula lies roughly 3800 light-years away, according to the caption.

understand.summary: Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 imaged the nebula in visible and near-infrared light, using filters for oxygen, hydrogen, nitrogen and iron emission; the colour mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: Several filters isolate single gases and some record near-infrared light, so the colours represent chemistry rather than what the eye would see.

behind.people: See full credit: NASA, ESA, and J. Kastner (RIT)

explore: From wingtip to wingtip the butterfly spans over two light-years, roughly half the gap between the Sun and Proxima Centauri, our nearest stellar neighbour.
alt: A glowing, butterfly-shaped nebula with jets and bubbles of gas.
